name: Schema Validation
description: Parses every JSON-LD block, resolves @id references, walks every typed node (including nested ones) and validates known types against required-field rules. Broken or incomplete structured data is ignored or misread by AI engines and rich-result parsers, so valid markup is what actually gets used.

scoring.summary: Page scope. No JSON-LD blocks -> 0. Only template-built blocks that cannot be parsed from source -> 3, inconclusive. Otherwise start at 5; subtract 0.5 per block that fails JSON.parse; compute validationRate = round(100 * valid / validatable) over every typed node (nested included, each node once, typed references to a node defined on the page skipped) whose type has a validator; if no validatable node exists the rate is 100, but if no block parsed at all the rate is 0. Subtract 2 if rate < 50, 1 if rate < 80, 0.5 if rate < 100. Clamp at 0, round to 1 decimal; the engine floors to an integer. If template-built blocks could not be parsed and the score is below 3 it is raised to 3 (inconclusive).

rules.condition: zero script[type="application/ld+json"] elements
each block where JSON.parse(textContent) throws (after template-tag substitution; template-built blocks that still fail are not counted, see divergences)

validators resolve pure {"@id": X} references (mainEntity, acceptedAnswer, author, step, itemListElement, offers) against any node on the page that defines X; a typed node whose @id is defined more fully elsewhere on the page is a reference and is not validated on its own

every object with @type anywhere in a parsed block (top level, @graph items, nested objects and arrays), each object once by identity; an @type array yields one entry per distinct validator (e.g. Organization + LocalBusiness validates once)
validationRate < 50
rules.issue: Only N% of schemas pass validation

rules.condition: 50 <= validationRate < 80
80 <= validationRate < 100
validationRate == 100 (including when no node has a validator, as long as at least one block parsed)
score = floor(max(0, round(score*10)/10))
rules.examples: one parse error only -> 4; rate 80-99 -> 4; rate 50-79 -> 4; rate < 50 -> 3; rate < 50 plus 1 parse error -> 2; 2 parse errors -> 4; 3 parse errors -> 3; a single broken block and nothing else -> 2

rules.condition: Each rule below is an ISSUE (makes node invalid). Warnings never affect score. Types not listed return valid: null and are excluded from the rate (e.g. WebSite, WebPage, ImageObject, Offer, Question, Answer, HowToStep, ListItem, PostalAddress, SearchAction, Recipe, Event, Review, Dentist and any other LocalBusiness subtype not listed). Types are matched after stripping a leading http(s)://schema.org/.
node @type in: FAQPage. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: mainEntity missing or not an array (stops)

rules.condition: node @type in: HowTo. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: step missing or not an array (stops)
step missing both text and name

rules.condition: node @type in: Product. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: each offer (array or single) missing price (0 allowed), priceRange and lowPrice
aggregateRating present but missing ratingValue (0 allowed)

rules.condition: node @type in: Organization, Corporation, GovernmentOrganization, EducationalOrganization, MedicalOrganization, NGO, Airline, LocalBusiness, Restaurant, Store, MedicalBusiness, LegalService, FinancialService, FoodEstablishment, HealthAndBeautyBusiness, HomeAndConstructionBusiness, EntertainmentBusiness, AutomotiveBusiness. Any issue makes the node invalid
node @type in: Article, BlogPosting, NewsArticle, TechArticle. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: author (first element if array, after @id resolution) is an object without name
datePublished not ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD with optional time and zone)

rules.condition: node @type in: Person. Any issue makes the node invalid
node @type in: BreadcrumbList. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: itemListElement missing or not an array (stops)
each item missing position (falsy, so position 0 is an issue)
each item missing both name and item.name

rules.condition: node @type in: ItemList. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: itemListElement missing or not an array

rules.condition: node @type in: VideoObject. Any issue makes the node invalid
node @type in: Dataset. Any issue makes the node invalid

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule on the integer score: >= 80% (4-5) pass, >= 50% (3) warning, else fail. A single parse error with everything else valid is therefore pass (4), where the extension said warning.

detect.source_procedure: Script checks/structured-data/valid.mjs runs on every HTML page the site model loads (built output or static HTML), using lib/jsonld.mjs extractJsonLd(doc, { templates: true }) and lib/schema-validator.mjs (a port of the extension's SchemaValidator) validateNodes. For unbuilt framework sources, build first; runtime-injected JSON-LD is not visible.

parity.note: Full parity when JSON-LD is literal in templates or a build output is available. Partial when JSON-LD is assembled at runtime (SPA frameworks, tag managers, CMS plugins injecting JSON-LD), when values come from CMS/frontmatter (a missing headline or datePublished depends on per-post data), or when templates emit different blocks per page type. Template syntax inside literal blocks can make static JSON.parse fail where the rendered page parses fine, so template tags must be substituted before parsing, never counted as parse errors.

fix_summary: Fix JSON syntax and add missing required properties per validator (e.g. Organization.name, Article headline/author{name}/datePublished ISO date, Product name/image/description/offers{price,priceCurrency}, FAQPage Question/acceptedAnswer Answer text, BreadcrumbList position/name) in the JSON-LD source: layout templates, Astro/Next components, Hugo partials, Eleventy includes or index.html. Values drawn from existing page data; content like prices or answer text may need the user.

divergences.extension: If every block fails JSON.parse, validationRate defaults to 100, so only the 0.5-per-block penalty applies (one broken block alone scores 4).
divergences.plugin: If no block parses, validationRate is 0 (one broken block alone scores 2).
divergences.reason: Bug: a page whose only structured data is broken passed validation.

divergences.extension: After @id resolution a @graph node referenced from author/publisher is collected twice (graph item and nested copy), so it counts double in the rate; @type arrays count once per type.
divergences.plugin: Each node is validated once (by identity), once per distinct validator.
divergences.reason: Bug: double counting skewed the rate.

divergences.extension: @type must match exactly, so full IRIs like "https://schema.org/Organization" fall into Other.
divergences.plugin: A leading http(s)://schema.org/ is stripped before matching.
divergences.reason: Full IRIs are valid JSON-LD for the same type.

divergences.extension: isValidISO8601 is new Date(x) not NaN, so strings like "March 3, 2024" pass as ISO 8601.
divergences.plugin: datePublished and uploadDate must have the ISO 8601 shape (YYYY-MM-DD with optional time and zone) and parse as a date.
divergences.reason: The issue text says ISO 8601; the code accepted non-ISO dates (comment/code mismatch).

divergences.extension: HowTo steps must all be @type HowToStep; HowToSection groups make the HowTo invalid.
divergences.plugin: HowToSection steps are accepted and their itemListElement HowToStep items are validated and counted.
divergences.reason: HowToSection is valid schema.org and Google-supported; the extension penalized normal markup.

divergences.extension: Offer price 0 counts as missing (falsy check); AggregateOffer lowPrice is not accepted; aggregateRating ratingValue 0 is missing.
divergences.plugin: price 0, lowPrice and ratingValue 0 count as present.
divergences.reason: Free products and AggregateOffer are valid; falsy checks flagged normal content.

divergences.extension: Only the properties mainEntity, itemListElement, acceptedAnswer, author, publisher have pure {"@id"} references resolved, against @graph items and top-level objects.
divergences.plugin: Validators resolve pure {"@id"} references (also for HowTo step and offers) against any node on the page that defines that @id.
divergences.reason: Same intent (Yoast/Rank Math @graph pattern), applied consistently.

divergences.extension: A typed reference such as publisher {"@type": "Organization", "@id": "#org"} is validated on its own and is invalid for lacking name, even when #org is fully defined on the page.
divergences.plugin: When the same @id is defined more fully elsewhere on the page, the typed reference is not validated separately; the full definition is. Unresolvable references are still validated (extension behaviour).

divergences.extension: Status uses validationRate thresholds (pass only at 100% with no parse errors), independent of the score.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.

divergences.extension: Reads the rendered page, where template tags are already filled in.
divergences.plugin: Reads HTML from the repo. JSON-LD holding template tags ({{ }}, {% %}, <% %>, <? ?>) is parsed with the tags replaced by a placeholder that counts as a present value; the result is marked predicted. A block that still cannot be parsed is never counted as a JSON error: the check reports inconclusive with partial credit and asks for a build or a live check.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: template values are unknown in the repo, and unrendered syntax is not a real error.
